order.title: Lock with a green light for codes 2, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, 29 and a red light for codes 16, 22, 24, 26
order.spec: A lock with 5 switches a, b, c, d, e (a is the biggest digit of the binary number): the green light turns on only for the numbers 2, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15 or 29, the red light turns on only for the numbers 16, 22, 24 or 26, and for every other number both lights stay off.

definition_of_done: Functional correctness: Simulate all 32 possible input combinations (a,b,c,d,e with a as MSB). Verify that green output is logic HIGH iff the binary value is in {2, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, 29}, and logic LOW otherwise. Verify that red output is logic HIGH iff the binary value is in {16, 22, 24, 26}, and logic LOW otherwise. Verify that for all remaining 21 values, both outputs are LOW. Verify that green and red are never HIGH simultaneously.
Blueprint formatting (per lessons L001–L004):
- Every gate has a unique name (no duplicate identifiers such as 'or1' used for both a gate and an instance).
- Every gate has a valid type from the allowed set {AND, OR, XOR, NOT}, with exactly 2 inputs for AND/OR/XOR and exactly 1 input for NOT.
- Every gate has exactly one output signal.
- Every output signal (green, red) is driven by exactly one gate output and maps to a real port.
- All input ports are exactly a, b, c, d, e; all output ports are exactly green, red. No extra or missing ports.
- No broken library part references (e.g., no 'lock_or' with internally duplicated names, no 'inverter_in' runner errors, no port-name mismatches between declared inputs and actual port names).
- Gate count and connectivity respect the allowed gate set only.
- No unconnected inputs or floating outputs.

parts.name: lock_5bit_decoder
parts.spec: Combinational 5-input lock: green activates for binary values 2,7,8,10,13,15,29; red activates for 16,22,24,26; both off for all other values. Input a is the MSB of the 5-bit number abcde.
